        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" ../scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Reserve Windows browser connection capacity
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          netsh int ipv4 set dynamicport tcp start=10000 num=55535
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Failed to expand the Windows TCP client port range" }
          netsh int ipv4 show dynamicport tcp
      - name: Run and validate extended Chromium evidence
        run: |
          node ../scripts/evals/portable-runner.mjs
          node ../scripts/evals/browser-report.mjs eval-results/portable/chromium/extended/results.json
        env:
          EVAL_BROWSER: chromium
          EVAL_TIER: extended
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Diagnose Windows browser connection failures
        if: (failure() || cancelled()) && runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          netsh int ipv4 show dynamicport tcp
          Get-NetTCPConnection | Group-Object State | Select-Object Count, Name | Format-Table
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: extended-chromium-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: frontend/eval-results/portable/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  firefox-extended:
    if: needs.scope.outputs.full == 'true'
    needs: [scope]
    name: Firefox portable UI
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" ../scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps firefox
      - run: node ../scripts/evals/portable-runner.mjs
        env:
          EVAL_BROWSER: firefox
          EVAL_TIER: ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.extended)) && 'extended' || 'core' }}
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Validate complete Firefox evidence
        run: node ../scripts/evals/browser-report.mjs eval-results/portable/firefox/${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.extended)) && 'extended' || 'core' }}/results.json
        env:
          EVAL_BROWSER: firefox
          EVAL_TIER: ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.extended)) && 'extended' || 'core' }}
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: portable-ui-linux-firefox-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: frontend/eval-results/portable/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  ui-gate:
    name: Playwright UI E2E
    needs: [linux, desktop, coverage, packs, portable-evidence, portable, chromium-extended, firefox-extended, scope]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
          upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      - name: Require complete selected UI matrices
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        env:
          LINUX: ${{ needs.linux.result }}
          DESKTOP: ${{ needs.desktop.result }}
          COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage.result }}
          PACKS: ${{ needs.packs.result }}
          CHROMIUM: ${{ needs.portable-evidence.result }}
          PORTABLE: ${{ needs.portable.result }}
          EXTENDED_CHROMIUM: ${{ needs.chromium-extended.result }}
          FIREFOX: ${{ needs.firefox-extended.result }}
          EXTENDED: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.extended) }}
        run: |
          test "$LINUX" = success
          test "$DESKTOP" = success
          test "$COVERAGE" = success
          test "$PACKS" = success
          test "$CHROMIUM" = success
          test "$PORTABLE" = success
          test "$FIREFOX" = success
          if [ "$EXTENDED" = true ]; then
            test "$EXTENDED_CHROMIUM" = success
          else
            test "$EXTENDED_CHROMIUM" = skipped
          fi
name: Sanitizers

# Memory-safety / leak guardrail: runs the pure-Rust core test suite under
# AddressSanitizer (ASan, which embeds LeakSanitizer) so a genuine leak or
# use-after-free in the protocol core fails the build.
#
# Scope: ONLY `mesh-talk-core --lib` (the UI-free core). The Tauri app links
# GTK/WebKit C libraries whose internals trip ASan with false positives we can't
# fix from here, so the app is deliberately excluded.
#
# Run on PRs targeting main so branch protection can require this memory-safety
# check before merge. Run again on main so the README badge reflects the merged
# code; keep the weekly run to catch toolchain and dependency drift.
# ASan needs the nightly toolchain + `-Z build-std` (a full std rebuild).
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Mondays 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

# Read-only: just checks out and runs the test suite under the sanitizer.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUSTFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
  RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-Zsanitizer=address"
  ASAN_OPTIONS: "detect_leaks=1"
  RUST_TEST_THREADS: "1"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

jobs:
  scope:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci-scope.yml

  cohort:
    if: needs.scope.outputs.full == 'true'
    needs: [scope]
    name: Build ASan test archive
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      toolchain: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
      rustc: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
      cargo: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
      archive_sha256: ${{ steps.build.outputs.archive_sha256 }}
      manifest_sha256: ${{ steps.build.outputs.manifest_sha256 }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        id: runner_storage
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Resolve installed nightly manifest
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          components: rust-src
      - name: Publish exact installed nightly cohort
        id: cohort
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs cohort
      - name: Install exact producer nightly cohort
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
          components: rust-src
      - name: Cache Rust build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          # Preserve the compatible cache prefix after moving compilation jobs.
          shared-key: sanitizers-shards
      - name: Install pinned Nextest
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.87.31
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.150
      - name: Verify pinned ASan archive protocol
        run: node --test scripts/ci/asan-cli.test.mjs
      - name: Compile and seal the ASan core archive once
        id: build
        env:
          MESH_ASAN_TOOLCHAIN: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
          MESH_ASAN_RUSTC: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
          MESH_ASAN_CARGO: ${{ steps.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs build tmp/asan-build
      - name: Upload this attempt's compiled ASan archive
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: asan-build-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: tmp/asan-build/
          compression-level: 0
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  shards:
    if: needs.scope.outputs.full == 'true'
    name: ASan core shard (${{ matrix.shard }}/8)
    needs: [cohort, scope]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
    env:
      MESH_ASAN_TOOLCHAIN: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
      MESH_ASAN_RUSTC: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
      MESH_ASAN_CARGO: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
      MESH_ASAN_ARCHIVE_SHA256: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.archive_sha256 }}
      MESH_ASAN_MANIFEST_SHA256: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.manifest_sha256 }}
      # Keep production case budgets and one instrumented test per runner.
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Install exact nightly cohort
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
          components: rust-src
      - name: Install pinned Nextest
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.87.31
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.150
      - name: Download the current compiled ASan archive
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: asan-build-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: tmp/asan-build
      # Both controls use the same instrumented std target as the real core.
      # A genuine ASan diagnosis must fail the intentional use-after-free.
      - name: Prove actual AddressSanitizer instrumentation
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs smoke tmp/asan-evidence
      - name: Test serial ASan partition
        env:
          MESH_ASAN_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs shard "$MESH_ASAN_SHARD" tmp/asan-evidence
      - name: Preserve ASan inventory and raw execution evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: asan-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: tmp/asan-evidence/
          if-no-files-found: error

  asan:
    name: ASan + LeakSanitizer (core)
    needs: [cohort, shards, scope]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      MESH_ASAN_TOOLCHAIN: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.toolchain }}
      MESH_ASAN_RUSTC: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.rustc }}
      MESH_ASAN_CARGO: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.cargo }}
      MESH_ASAN_ARCHIVE_SHA256: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.archive_sha256 }}
      MESH_ASAN_MANIFEST_SHA256: ${{ needs.cohort.outputs.manifest_sha256 }}
      MESH_ASAN_SHARDS_RESULT: ${{ needs.shards.result }}
      MESH_ASAN_BUILD_RESULT: ${{ needs.cohort.result }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
          upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Download this attempt's ASan evidence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: asan-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-shard-*
          path: tmp/asan-union
      - name: Verify every actual shard and complete exact-source union
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node scripts/ci/asan.mjs verify tmp/asan-union
name: Native core workflow evaluation

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      full:
        type: string
        default: 'true'
      upstream_result:
        type: string
        default: success
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  native:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    name: Real native UI (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2022, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') == 'true' && matrix.os || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ (inputs.full || 'true') }}
          upstream_result: ${{ inputs.upstream_result || 'success' }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        id: runner_storage
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          # Keep compiled dependencies when a scenario fails, not its verdict.
          cache-on-failure: true
      - name: Diagnose multicast on the actual native test runner
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node scripts/diagnostics/native-multicast-probe.mjs
      - name: Route the fixture multicast group locally (macOS runner only)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'macOS') }}
        run: |
          sudo route -n add -host 224.0.0.167 -interface 127.0.0.1
          node scripts/diagnostics/native-multicast-probe.mjs --require
      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs
      - name: Linux native webview dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libssl-dev xvfb openbox dbus-x11 xdotool fonts-noto-cjk fonts-noto-color-emoji
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci
      - name: Verify fail-closed evidence validator
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node --test scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts-report.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/png-evidence.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/native-core-scenarios.test.mjs
      - name: Build source-pinned frontend, production app, CLI and native driver
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: node scripts/validation/native-build.mjs
      - name: Run native evaluation (Linux desktop session)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        env:
          NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Native focus and screenshot assertions require a real window manager.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2016
          xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1200x24' dbus-run-session -- bash -e -c '
            mkdir -p "$NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT"
            openbox > "$NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT/openbox.log" 2>&1 &
            node scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts.mjs
          '
      - name: Run native evaluation (Windows and macOS desktop)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os != 'Linux') }}
        env:
          NATIVE_CONTACT_OUTPUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: node scripts/diagnostics/hidden-contacts.mjs
      - name: Upload native evidence even on failure
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always()) }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: native-core-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Publish evidence only, never fixture keystores or account data.
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.png
            ${{ runner.temp }}/hidden-contacts-native/*.log
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
// Direct execution checks shared by release acceptance and the one-time protection
// migration. PR-only and main-only policies deliberately remain separate.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";

import { windowsPartitions as nativePartitions } from "./windows-coverage.mjs";

const windowsPartitions = nativePartitions.map(shard => `windows / Windows workspace tests (${shard}/${nativePartitions.length})`);
const windows = ["windows / Windows workspace build", ...windowsPartitions];
const workspace = [...["ubuntu-latest", "macos-latest"].map(os => `checks (${os})`), ...windows];
const health = ["health / Source and supply-chain checks", ...["ubuntu-latest", "macos-26-intel", "windows-latest"].map(os => `health / Portable checks (${os})`)];
const backend = ["windows-2022", "macos-26-intel"].map(os => `Backend core (${os})`);
const native = ["ubuntu-24.04", "windows-2022", "macos-latest"].map(os => `native-core / Real native UI (${os})`);

export const releaseSourceChecks = Object.freeze([
  ...workspace, ...health, ...backend, ...native,
  "Playwright UI E2E", "ASan + LeakSanitizer (core)", "mutants", "scan", "Scorecard analysis",
  "Analyze (rust)", "Analyze (actions)", "Analyze (javascript-typescript)",
]);

// Top-level workflow ownership: reusable jobs belong to their caller's suite.
export const releaseSourceWorkflows = Object.freeze({
  ...Object.fromEntries(workspace.map(name => [name, ".github/workflows/ci.yml"])),
  ...Object.fromEntries(health.map(name => [name, ".github/workflows/e2e-ui.yml"])),
  ...Object.fromEntries([...backend, ...native].map(name => [name, ".github/workflows/e2e-backend.yml"])),
  "Playwright UI E2E": ".github/workflows/e2e-ui.yml",
  "ASan + LeakSanitizer (core)": ".github/workflows/sanitizers.yml",
  mutants: ".github/workflows/mutants.yml",
  scan: ".github/workflows/gitleaks.yml",
  "Scorecard analysis": ".github/workflows/scorecard.yml",
  ...Object.fromEntries(["rust", "actions", "javascript-typescript"].map(language => [`Analyze (${language})`, ".github/workflows/codeql.yml"])),
});

export function pendingSuccessfulChecks(checks, names, appSlug = "github-actions") {
  assert.ok(Array.isArray(checks), "source checks must be an array");
  return names.filter(name => {
    const latest = checks.filter(check => check.name === name && check.app?.slug === appSlug).sort((a, b) => b.id - a.id)[0];
    if (!latest || latest.status !== "completed") return true;
    assert.equal(latest.conclusion, "success", `required source check not successful: ${name}`);
    return false;
  });
}

export function requireSuccessfulChecks(checks, names, appSlug) {
  const pending = pendingSuccessfulChecks(checks, names, appSlug);
  assert.equal(pending.length, 0, `required source check not successful: ${pending.join(", ")}`);
}

const replacements = new Map([
  ["verify", workspace],
  ["checks (windows-latest)", windows],
  ...[1, 2].map(shard => [`windows / Windows workspace tests (${shard}/2)`, windowsPartitions]),
  ...[1, 2, 3, 4].map(shard => [`windows / Windows workspace tests (${shard}/4)`, windowsPartitions]),
  ["health / Portable checks (macos-latest)", ["health / Portable checks (macos-26-intel)"]],
  ["Backend core (macos-latest)", ["Backend core (macos-26-intel)"]],
  ["Portable UI (macos-latest, webkit)", ["Portable UI (macos-26-intel, webkit)"]],
  ["Backend core (ubuntu-24.04)", ["checks (ubuntu-latest)"]],
  ["Multi-process E2E", ["checks (ubuntu-latest)", ...backend, ...native]],
  ...["ubuntu-latest", "macos-latest", "windows-latest"].map(os => [`Code Quality and Health Check (${os})`, health]),
  ...["ubuntu-24.04", "windows-2022", "macos-latest"].map(os => [`native-core / Runner multicast diagnostic (${os})`, [`native-core / Real native UI (${os})`]]),
  ...["ubuntu-24.04", "windows-2022", "macos-latest"].map(os => [`Portable UI (${os}, chromium)`, ["Chromium portable evidence"]]),
]);

export function migrateRequiredChecks(current) {
  assert.equal(typeof current.strict, "boolean", "protection strictness is required");
  assert.ok(Array.isArray(current.checks) && current.checks.length, "app-bound required checks are required");
  const migrated = new Map();
  for (const check of current.checks) {
    assert.ok(typeof check.context === "string" && Number.isInteger(check.app_id), "invalid required check app binding");
    for (const context of replacements.get(check.context) ?? [check.context]) {
      const prior = migrated.get(context);
      assert.ok(!prior || prior.app_id === check.app_id, `conflicting check app binding: ${context}`);
      migrated.set(context, { context, app_id: check.app_id });
    }
  }
  return { strict: current.strict, checks: [...migrated.values()].sort((a, b) => a.context.localeCompare(b.context, "en")) };
}

export function requireProtectionEvidence(policy, checks) {
  for (const { context, app_id: appId } of policy.checks) {
    const latest = checks.filter(check => check.name === context && check.app?.id === appId).sort((a, b) => b.id - a.id)[0];
    assert.ok(latest?.status === "completed" && latest.conclusion === "success", `required replacement check has no successful current-source app-bound evidence: ${context}`);
  }

import path from "node:path";
import { readFile, realpath, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
import { rustPackages } from "../pr-platform/rust-packages.mjs";

export const contractFiles = [
  "scripts/validation/validation.json",
  "frontend/validation.json",
  ...rustPackages.map(({ directory }) => `${directory}/validation.json`),
];

/** Read a regular repository file without following a symlink outside root. */
export async function readRepositoryFile(root, file) {
  if (
    typeof file !== "string" ||
    !file ||
    path.isAbsolute(file) ||
    file.split("/").includes("..") ||
    /[\\\x00-\x1f\x7f]/u.test(file)
  )
    throw Error(`Unsafe repository path: ${file}`);
  const base = await realpath(root);
  const resolved = await realpath(path.resolve(base, file));
  const relative = path.relative(base, resolved);
  if (
    !relative ||
    relative === ".." ||
    relative.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) ||
    path.isAbsolute(relative)
  )
    throw Error(`Repository path escapes root: ${file}`);
  if (!(await stat(resolved)).isFile())
    throw Error(`Not a regular file: ${file}`);
  return readFile(resolved, "utf8");
}

export async function loadContracts(root) {
  const contracts = [];
  for (const file of contractFiles) {
    try {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(await readRepositoryFile(root, file));
      if (parsed.schema !== 1 || !Array.isArray(parsed.contracts))
        throw Error("expected schema 1 and a contracts array");
      contracts.push(...parsed.contracts);
    } catch (error) {
      throw Error(`Invalid validation contract: ${file}: ${error.message}`);
    }
  }
  return contracts;
}

name: Tauri Release

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "23 3 * * *"
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*" # Triggered when pushing tags
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish_nightly:
        description: Build and publish a verified Nightly prerelease from main
        type: boolean
        default: false
      publish_release:
        description: Publish the verified draft (select a version tag, not a branch)
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || inputs.publish_nightly) && 'nightly' || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  preflight:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 250
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      checks: read
      security-events: read
    outputs:
      nightly: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.nightly }}
      skip: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.skip }}
      tag: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Validate source, version and draft state
        id: inputs
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_NIGHTLY: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || inputs.publish_nightly }}
          RELEASE_PUBLICATION: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.publish_release }}
        run: node scripts/release/preflight.mjs
      - name: Wait for successful exact-source CI before Nightly compilation
        if: steps.inputs.outputs.nightly == 'true' && steps.inputs.outputs.skip != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node scripts/release/check-source-checks.mjs "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_SHA" --wait

  build-release:
    needs: preflight
    if: inputs.publish_release != true && needs.preflight.outputs.skip != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    env:
      ARTIFACT_TAG: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.tag }}
      # Free updater keys are available only to the existing trusted publication sources.
      MESH_TALK_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) && vars.MESH_TALK_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY || '' }}
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) && secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY || '' }}
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) && secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD || '' }}
      MESH_TALK_BUILD_TAG: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && needs.preflight.outputs.tag || format('v{0}-dev', needs.preflight.outputs.version) }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target:
          - x86_64-apple-darwin
          - aarch64-apple-darwin
          - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
          - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
        include:
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-11-arm
            target: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
          - os: linux
            # Keep the AppImage glibc baseline aligned with Linux ARM64.

name: Tauri Release

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "23 3 * * *"
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*" # Triggered when pushing tags
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish_nightly:
        description: Build and publish a verified Nightly prerelease from main
        type: boolean
        default: false
      publish_release:
        description: Publish the verified draft (select a version tag, not a branch)
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || inputs.publish_nightly) && 'nightly' || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  preflight:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 250
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      checks: read
      security-events: read
    outputs:
      nightly: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.nightly }}
      skip: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.skip }}
      tag: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.inputs.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Validate source, version and draft state
        id: inputs
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_NIGHTLY: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || inputs.publish_nightly }}
          RELEASE_PUBLICATION: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.publish_release }}
        run: node scripts/release/preflight.mjs
      - name: Wait for successful exact-source CI before Nightly compilation
        if: steps.inputs.outputs.nightly == 'true' && steps.inputs.outputs.skip != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node scripts/release/check-source-checks.mjs "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_SHA" --wait

  build-release:
    needs: preflight
    if: inputs.publish_release != true && needs.preflight.outputs.skip != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    env:
      ARTIFACT_TAG: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.tag }}
      # Free updater keys are available only to the existing trusted publication sources.
      MESH_TALK_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) && vars.MESH_TALK_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY || '' }}
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) && secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY || '' }}
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) && secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD || '' }}
      MESH_TALK_BUILD_TAG: ${{ (needs.preflight.outputs.nightly == 'true' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && needs.preflight.outputs.tag || format('v{0}-dev', needs.preflight.outputs.version) }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target:
          - x86_64-apple-darwin
          - aarch64-apple-darwin
          - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
          - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
        include:
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-11-arm
            target: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
          - os: linux
            # Keep the AppImage glibc baseline aligned with Linux ARM64.

# Keeping CI fast and reliable

Treat feedback time, reliability and resource use as maintained requirements.
Every feature, dependency and test can change CI cost, even without a workflow
edit. AI agents and contributors should preserve useful coverage while reducing
unnecessary work, and leave failures easier to reproduce and diagnose.

This guide owns CI maintenance decisions and regression prevention. It does not
introduce another workflow, command catalog or acceptance policy.

| Question                                            | Authoritative owner                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which tests, commands and CI jobs apply?            | [Testing feedback loop](testing-feedback-loop.md), owning `validation.json` contracts and [workflow definitions](../.github/workflows/) |
| What evidence permits acceptance or release?        | [Quality gates](quality-gates.md) and [version and release lifecycle](updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)                       |
| Where does an implementation or shared rule belong? | [Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) and [script entry points](../scripts/README.md)                                                |
| Which consumers and documentation need updating?    | [Change alignment checklist](maintenance-checklist.md) and [documentation guidelines](DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md)                      |

Keep tool versions, matrix sizes, deadlines, cache keys and required-check names
in their existing executable owners. Keep run histories and investigation output
in ignored `tmp/` or PR/CI artifacts; durable decisions belong in the owning guide.

## Make the cost of a change explicit

Before adding a suite, fixture, dependency, platform or workflow, identify the
existing owner and the observable failure it must detect. Inspect the affected
plan and consumers through the [validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities).
Answer four questions in the change when they are material:

- What requirement needs new evidence, and why is existing evidence insufficient?
- Which layer and platform can exercise that requirement faithfully?
- What recurring setup, compilation, execution and artifact cost will it add?
- Can an existing task, fixture or compatible output supply it without weakening
  assertions or introducing another owner for the same rule?

Extend the existing implementation first. Share policy and lifecycle rules where
their meaning is identical; keep feature-specific fixtures local. An abstraction
is useful when it removes duplicated decisions and has clear inputs, outputs and
failure behavior. Avoid both copied shell fragments and a generic CI framework
whose configuration is harder to review than the work it coordinates.

Do not make a full local suite the default for every edit. Use affected feedback
while developing, then complete the applicable boundary and candidate gates.
New tests still need independent assertions; matching the implementation or
increasing a test count does not establish useful coverage.

## Keep workflow policy thin and reject cheap failures locally

Workflows own triggers, permissions, runners, matrices, dependencies and artifact
transport. Scripts own inventory validation, artifact roles, packaging, report
collection and execution policy. Reuse the same CLI locally and in Actions;
extract substantial conditionals and loops into the existing feature owner rather
than copying YAML fragments or introducing another generic orchestration layer.
When moving execution into a script, update every caller and smoke check. Keep
launcher behavior in its owning regression instead of requiring obsolete command
text in YAML. Cross-platform filesystem paths use `fileURLToPath` rather than
`.pathname`; ESM module arguments retain a file URL or relative module specifier
instead of a native Windows absolute path. Exercise each boundary on its platform.
Keep live source/release checks immediately before each publication boundary;
those protect against changed state and are not redundant setup checks.

The [syntax owner](../scripts/validation/syntax.mjs) parses changed Node, Bash and
Python sources without executing them or writing Python caches, and invokes
`actionlint` for changed workflows. Pre-commit selects staged paths but checks
worktree bytes, matching the existing structural checks. Affected validation also
checks new nonignored sources; PR creation checks the clean committed comparison.
Use Node 22, Bash and Python; install actionlint before changing workflows. No
checker installs tools or contacts the network. Hook installation configures hooks
without launching comprehensive health; request that gate explicitly.

PR creation runs `make pr-check`'s cheap-check owner against its actual comparison
base, rejects ownership blockers and checks applicable frontend patch coverage
before publication. Version projections, contract references and hygiene already
belong to structural standards; reuse that owner rather than adding duplicate
gates. Do not install dependencies, compile Rust, launch browsers or run application suites
implicitly in the cheap mode. Source changes during checking invalidate it.
Workflow edits also run the existing fast CI policy owner locally. Configuration
assertions and runner inventory discovery belong here; application execution and
native compiler fixtures do not. Update the existing policy assertion when its
requirement changes instead of adding a second overlapping test in another file.
For entry-point changes, also run the affected contract tests selected by the
existing validation plan before publication. A syntax pass or a hand-picked
filename sample cannot detect stale semantic routing expectations; cheap PR
checks do not certify those tests passed.

The frontend precheck reads the target from `codecov.yml`, includes partially
covered branches in the uncovered denominator and rejects omitted changed files.
Exercise report readers against actual producer output as well as small fixtures;
negative V8 branch counts remain uncovered rather than invalidating the report.
It verifies an existing clean-candidate `frontend-coverage` receipt through the
canonical stage owner and rechecks LCOV bytes, rather than trusting a timestamp or
raw report. Generate missing evidence explicitly with the reported command. A
verification-only miss never starts coverage, waits for a heavy lock or claims a
pass; a no-work verification lease must not imply admitted child work. Keep
verified scope termination diagnostics separate from the actual test result.
This frontend unit precheck is conservative; Rust and browser-union coverage
still need their owning evidence. Native execution, dependency resolution and
published-asset verification cannot be replaced by parsing or stale build output.

Use the existing package inventory's `frontendBuild` ownership when preparing
Rust selectors. Core, integrations and MCP selections still require real target
validation, but do not build frontend assets merely because Rust changed. Host
selections must still prepare Tauri's `frontendDist` before selector discovery.

Composed local gates must invoke shared stages through the same canonical command
and full-mode environment. Normalize `FAST=0` in both full-preflight children so
equivalent successful stages can reuse their verified receipts; do not weaken
identity checks or mutate the caller's environment to manufacture a cache hit.

Local feedback does not replace committed-candidate acceptance. Git documents
that [hooks can be bypassed](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks); web edits and other
# Quality gates and release evidence

The gate verifies outcomes, not just process exit codes. A successful compiler,
high line coverage, or a browser mock is not proof of a correct native release.
Keep implementation plans and transient verification logs outside the repository.

## Change review

Prefer independently reviewable PRs with one feature or mechanism. Record the exact
tested commit, executed commands, failing-baseline evidence, native runner links,
and limitations in the PR. Follow the [validation stages](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
for affected feedback and boundary evidence; comprehensive local preparation is
optional, and current-candidate protected CI remains required before merge.
Use the existing [PR preparation entry point](testing-feedback-loop.md#fast-pr-creation-and-optional-full-local-preparation)
when comprehensive local evidence is needed. The full health gate builds frontend
assets before Tauri compilation, including on a fresh checkout.

[CI maintenance](ci-maintenance.md) owns efficiency and reliability decisions.
Gate scope, evidence requirements and release acceptance remain owned here;
an optimization proposal does not itself authorize reducing them.

For each applicable scenario, assert externally observable outcomes. A test should
fail with the old implementation or a deliberate incorrect mutation. Do not weaken
assertions to accommodate unexplained failures.

| Change                 | Required scenarios in addition to the happy path                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Persistent state       | Reopen/restart, append after torn record, read/write failure, owner isolation, no memory-only success after failed persistence |
| Permissions/privacy    | Allow and deny, revocation after existing session, restart recovery, unknown peer/device, group vs direct-message boundaries   |
| Async UI/media         | Account switch/logout while request is pending, late response rejection, failed save and retry, media cleanup                  |
| Multiple devices/files | Every destination, one logical history record, sender restart before recipient download, revoked access                        |
| Platform/native UI     | Real Tauri IPC and window/process state on the affected OS, negative control, runner/desktop/GPU limitations                   |
| CI/release scripts     | Real fixture files, missing/partial evidence, tool failures, changed source and stale artifacts                                |

Rust unit/integration, real multi-process backend E2E, browser UI tests, and native
desktop tests answer different questions. A VM/Xvfb/software-renderer pass does not
establish that a reported physical GPU or VMware compositor fault is fixed.

## Test quality and evidence

`node --test scripts/diagnostics/*.test.mjs` runs in three-platform CI and the health
gate. Python 3.11+ is required for archive regressions; CI pins Python 3.12. The
diagnostic suite includes actual release-script execution with deliberate verifier
failures, real ZIP corruption fixtures, and release-state changes after verification.
Full health requires cargo-deny, cargo-machete, typos, Gitleaks, ShellCheck and
actionlint; missing tools fail rather than being silently skipped. CI installs them
explicitly. `--fast` remains a clearly labeled partial local check.

For full-scope candidates, Health runs inside the UI orchestrator for every PR and
merge candidate, and independently on its weekly/manual triggers. All three
platform diagnostic suites remain mandatory. The complete frontend unit suite
runs once with coverage on Linux; its platform branches use explicit mocks,
while real browser/native behavior retains the platform matrices. Source-only
formatting, type/lint and dependency policy run once. The Linux coverage producer seals
its line map for same-run UI consumers; source, workflow, run, attempt and digest
must all match. Superseded PR and merge candidates are cancelled automatically. Every main push
has its own verification group, preserving pending commits for release evidence.
Health uses a distinct caller-workflow/event namespace, so independent manual or
scheduled runs cannot cancel the UI caller or its same-run evidence producer.

Inert documentation PRs may omit unrelated product execution only after the
[documentation scope owner](ci-maintenance.md#documentation-only-pr-scope)
proves eligibility against the exact tested merge. Required check identities
remain present and validate that decision; their success means the product work
is not applicable, not that its tests ran. Applicable documentation and security
checks still run. Failed selection, mixed changes and authority inputs cannot
qualify. Main pushes, merge groups, schedules and manual runs retain complete
execution. Release consumers require checks from the owning successful trusted
main-push workflow suite, never PR-only scope decisions.

Branch protection requires direct execution checks instead of runner-backed
copies of their aggregate result. `scripts/ci/required-checks.mjs` owns the direct
release policy and replacement mapping. Source and all platform checks are
individually required; Windows requires its build producer and all archive
consumers. Release acceptance uses the same direct names plus its main-only
checks, including ASan and mutation-runner acceptance. A newer failed, pending or
missing check still rejects the exact source. Stable repeats this strict check
immediately before public container upload and final release publication, after
lengthy preparation; Nightly retains its final strict recheck. To inspect a migration, run
`node scripts/ci/migrate-required-checks.mjs OWNER/REPO main PR_NUMBER --plan`.
Use `--apply` only after the replacement checks pass on the current PR head. The
command validates each bound GitHub App, rejects a changed candidate/policy,
preserves strictness and unrelated checks, and verifies the readback. A missing
old context before migration is pending, never permission to bypass a gate.
Diagnostics run on the actual native test machine; a probe on another VM cannot
certify that machine's network capability. Windows gates explicitly use Bash;
opening a script through a file association does not establish execution.

Mutation testing uses pinned cargo-mutants 27.1.0 and examines all Rust workspace
members on daily and manual runs. PR, push and merge-queue runs validate the pinned

Treat feedback time, reliability and resource use as maintained requirements.
Every feature, dependency and test can change CI cost, even without a workflow
edit. AI agents and contributors should preserve useful coverage while reducing
unnecessary work, and leave failures easier to reproduce and diagnose.

This guide owns CI maintenance decisions and regression prevention. It does not
introduce another workflow, command catalog or acceptance policy.

| Question                                            | Authoritative owner                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which tests, commands and CI jobs apply?            | [Testing feedback loop](testing-feedback-loop.md), owning `validation.json` contracts and [workflow definitions](../.github/workflows/) |
| What evidence permits acceptance or release?        | [Quality gates](quality-gates.md) and [version and release lifecycle](updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)                       |
| Where does an implementation or shared rule belong? | [Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) and [script entry points](../scripts/README.md)                                                |
| Which consumers and documentation need updating?    | [Change alignment checklist](maintenance-checklist.md) and [documentation guidelines](DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md)                      |

Keep tool versions, matrix sizes, deadlines, cache keys and required-check names
in their existing executable owners. Keep run histories and investigation output
in ignored `tmp/` or PR/CI artifacts; durable decisions belong in the owning guide.

## Make the cost of a change explicit

Before adding a suite, fixture, dependency, platform or workflow, identify the
existing owner and the observable failure it must detect. Inspect the affected
plan and consumers through the [validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities).
Answer four questions in the change when they are material:

- What requirement needs new evidence, and why is existing evidence insufficient?
- Which layer and platform can exercise that requirement faithfully?
- What recurring setup, compilation, execution and artifact cost will it add?
- Can an existing task, fixture or compatible output supply it without weakening
  assertions or introducing another owner for the same rule?

Extend the existing implementation first. Share policy and lifecycle rules where
their meaning is identical; keep feature-specific fixtures local. An abstraction
is useful when it removes duplicated decisions and has clear inputs, outputs and
failure behavior. Avoid both copied shell fragments and a generic CI framework
whose configuration is harder to review than the work it coordinates.

Do not make a full local suite the default for every edit. Use affected feedback
while developing, then complete the applicable boundary and candidate gates.
New tests still need independent assertions; matching the implementation or
increasing a test count does not establish useful coverage.

## Keep workflow policy thin and reject cheap failures locally

Workflows own triggers, permissions, runners, matrices, dependencies and artifact
transport. Scripts own inventory validation, artifact roles, packaging, report
collection and execution policy. Reuse the same CLI locally and in Actions;
extract substantial conditionals and loops into the existing feature owner rather
than copying YAML fragments or introducing another generic orchestration layer.
When moving execution into a script, update every caller and smoke check. Keep
launcher behavior in its owning regression instead of requiring obsolete command
text in YAML. Cross-platform filesystem paths use `fileURLToPath` rather than
`.pathname`; ESM module arguments retain a file URL or relative module specifier
instead of a native Windows absolute path. Exercise each boundary on its platform.
Keep live source/release checks immediately before each publication boundary;
those protect against changed state and are not redundant setup checks.

The [syntax owner](../scripts/validation/syntax.mjs) parses changed Node, Bash and
Python sources without executing them or writing Python caches, and invokes
`actionlint` for changed workflows. Pre-commit selects staged paths but checks
worktree bytes, matching the existing structural checks. Affected validation also
checks new nonignored sources; PR creation checks the clean committed comparison.
Use Node 22, Bash and Python; install actionlint before changing workflows. No
checker installs tools or contacts the network. Hook installation configures hooks
without launching comprehensive health; request that gate explicitly.

PR creation runs `make pr-check`'s cheap-check owner against its actual comparison
base, rejects ownership blockers and checks applicable frontend patch coverage
before publication. Version projections, contract references and hygiene already
belong to structural standards; reuse that owner rather than adding duplicate
gates. Do not install dependencies, compile Rust, launch browsers or run application suites
implicitly in the cheap mode. Source changes during checking invalidate it.
Workflow edits also run the existing fast CI policy owner locally. Configuration
assertions and runner inventory discovery belong here; application execution and
native compiler fixtures do not. Update the existing policy assertion when its
requirement changes instead of adding a second overlapping test in another file.
For entry-point changes, also run the affected contract tests selected by the
existing validation plan before publication. A syntax pass or a hand-picked
filename sample cannot detect stale semantic routing expectations; cheap PR
checks do not certify those tests passed.

The frontend precheck reads the target from `codecov.yml`, includes partially
covered branches in the uncovered denominator and rejects omitted changed files.
Exercise report readers against actual producer output as well as small fixtures;
negative V8 branch counts remain uncovered rather than invalidating the report.
It verifies an existing clean-candidate `frontend-coverage` receipt through the
canonical stage owner and rechecks LCOV bytes, rather than trusting a timestamp or
raw report. Generate missing evidence explicitly with the reported command. A
verification-only miss never starts coverage, waits for a heavy lock or claims a
pass; a no-work verification lease must not imply admitted child work. Keep
verified scope termination diagnostics separate from the actual test result.
This frontend unit precheck is conservative; Rust and browser-union coverage
still need their owning evidence. Native execution, dependency resolution and
published-asset verification cannot be replaced by parsing or stale build output.

Use the existing package inventory's `frontendBuild` ownership when preparing
Rust selectors. Core, integrations and MCP selections still require real target
validation, but do not build frontend assets merely because Rust changed. Host
selections must still prepare Tauri's `frontendDist` before selector discovery.

Composed local gates must invoke shared stages through the same canonical command
and full-mode environment. Normalize `FAST=0` in both full-preflight children so
equivalent successful stages can reuse their verified receipts; do not weaken
identity checks or mutate the caller's environment to manufacture a cache hit.

Local feedback does not replace committed-candidate acceptance. Git documents
that [hooks can be bypassed](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks); web edits and other
# Quality gates and release evidence

The gate verifies outcomes, not just process exit codes. A successful compiler,
high line coverage, or a browser mock is not proof of a correct native release.
Keep implementation plans and transient verification logs outside the repository.

## Change review

Prefer independently reviewable PRs with one feature or mechanism. Record the exact
tested commit, executed commands, failing-baseline evidence, native runner links,
and limitations in the PR. Follow the [validation stages](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
for affected feedback and boundary evidence; comprehensive local preparation is
optional, and current-candidate protected CI remains required before merge.
Use the existing [PR preparation entry point](testing-feedback-loop.md#fast-pr-creation-and-optional-full-local-preparation)
when comprehensive local evidence is needed. The full health gate builds frontend
assets before Tauri compilation, including on a fresh checkout.

[CI maintenance](ci-maintenance.md) owns efficiency and reliability decisions.
Gate scope, evidence requirements and release acceptance remain owned here;
an optimization proposal does not itself authorize reducing them.

For each applicable scenario, assert externally observable outcomes. A test should
fail with the old implementation or a deliberate incorrect mutation. Do not weaken
assertions to accommodate unexplained failures.

| Change                 | Required scenarios in addition to the happy path                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Persistent state       | Reopen/restart, append after torn record, read/write failure, owner isolation, no memory-only success after failed persistence |
| Permissions/privacy    | Allow and deny, revocation after existing session, restart recovery, unknown peer/device, group vs direct-message boundaries   |
| Async UI/media         | Account switch/logout while request is pending, late response rejection, failed save and retry, media cleanup                  |
| Multiple devices/files | Every destination, one logical history record, sender restart before recipient download, revoked access                        |
| Platform/native UI     | Real Tauri IPC and window/process state on the affected OS, negative control, runner/desktop/GPU limitations                   |
| CI/release scripts     | Real fixture files, missing/partial evidence, tool failures, changed source and stale artifacts                                |

Rust unit/integration, real multi-process backend E2E, browser UI tests, and native
desktop tests answer different questions. A VM/Xvfb/software-renderer pass does not
establish that a reported physical GPU or VMware compositor fault is fixed.

## Test quality and evidence

`node --test scripts/diagnostics/*.test.mjs` runs in three-platform CI and the health
gate. Python 3.11+ is required for archive regressions; CI pins Python 3.12. The
diagnostic suite includes actual release-script execution with deliberate verifier
failures, real ZIP corruption fixtures, and release-state changes after verification.
Full health requires cargo-deny, cargo-machete, typos, Gitleaks, ShellCheck and
actionlint; missing tools fail rather than being silently skipped. CI installs them
explicitly. `--fast` remains a clearly labeled partial local check.

For full-scope candidates, Health runs inside the UI orchestrator for every PR and
merge candidate, and independently on its weekly/manual triggers. All three
platform diagnostic suites remain mandatory. The complete frontend unit suite
runs once with coverage on Linux; its platform branches use explicit mocks,
while real browser/native behavior retains the platform matrices. Source-only
formatting, type/lint and dependency policy run once. The Linux coverage producer seals
its line map for same-run UI consumers; source, workflow, run, attempt and digest
must all match. Superseded PR and merge candidates are cancelled automatically. Every main push
has its own verification group, preserving pending commits for release evidence.
Health uses a distinct caller-workflow/event namespace, so independent manual or
scheduled runs cannot cancel the UI caller or its same-run evidence producer.

Inert documentation PRs may omit unrelated product execution only after the
[documentation scope owner](ci-maintenance.md#documentation-only-pr-scope)
proves eligibility against the exact tested merge. Required check identities
remain present and validate that decision; their success means the product work
is not applicable, not that its tests ran. Applicable documentation and security
checks still run. Failed selection, mixed changes and authority inputs cannot
qualify. Main pushes, merge groups, schedules and manual runs retain complete
execution. Release consumers require checks from the owning successful trusted
main-push workflow suite, never PR-only scope decisions.

Branch protection requires direct execution checks instead of runner-backed
copies of their aggregate result. `scripts/ci/required-checks.mjs` owns the direct
release policy and replacement mapping. Source and all platform checks are
individually required; Windows requires its build producer and all archive
consumers. Release acceptance uses the same direct names plus its main-only
checks, including ASan and mutation-runner acceptance. A newer failed, pending or
missing check still rejects the exact source. Stable repeats this strict check
immediately before public container upload and final release publication, after
lengthy preparation; Nightly retains its final strict recheck. To inspect a migration, run
`node scripts/ci/migrate-required-checks.mjs OWNER/REPO main PR_NUMBER --plan`.
Use `--apply` only after the replacement checks pass on the current PR head. The
command validates each bound GitHub App, rejects a changed candidate/policy,
preserves strictness and unrelated checks, and verifies the readback. A missing
old context before migration is pending, never permission to bypass a gate.
Diagnostics run on the actual native test machine; a probe on another VM cannot
certify that machine's network capability. Windows gates explicitly use Bash;
opening a script through a file association does not establish execution.

## R03: Actual work owns its lifetime

Consume the canonical process owner's result contract rather than deriving a new
verdict from a diagnostic flag. Windows atomically terminates its owned job even
when empty, so verified `forcedRetirement` alone does not mean work leaked or a
successful test failed. Preserve the actual exit status and error, cancellation,
timeout and cleanup-verification results. The empty-job owner control and UI
runner outcome controls exercise that distinction.

POSIX process-group retirement proves only that group. A browser framework may
launch its web server in another group; use the actual tool's teardown protocol
and retain independent server-retirement controls in the UI command owner. Missing
cooperative teardown evidence cannot become verified cleanup merely because the
CLI exited or its group disappeared.
Tools such as Nextest and cargo-mutants create independently grouped children.
Killing their supervisor can close captured output while a real test remains
alive. Trace the tool's actual child ownership and shutdown protocol; neither
pipe closure nor the original group's disappearance proves retirement. The
[Linux mutation owner](../scripts/release/mutation-process-owner.py) uses a kernel
subreaper, pidfd-verified direct-child authority and one reaping loop across
normal exit and cancellation. Child enumeration supplies candidates, not absence
proof; only kernel `ECHILD` after reaping establishes no owned descendants.
Missing, invalid or incomplete retirement acknowledgment keeps cleanup unverified.
Reserve the owner's bounded teardown window without changing ordinary callers'
defaults or using process names, stale PIDs or broad group sweeps as authority.
Actual direct-tool, nested-tool and active-build cancellation controls retain an
unrelated sibling and require acknowledged test retirement before returning.

Leader exit and output-pipe closure are separate lifecycle events. Bound draining
after owned-group retirement: an escaped descendant can retain inherited pipes
forever. Close only the owner's read ends, retain unverified cleanup and quarantine
its lease; the real detached-pipe natural-exit and cancellation controls exercise
this failure in the validation process owner.
Cleanup uncertainty is monotonic across cancellation and draining: successfully
retiring one group cannot clear an earlier unverified escaped-process boundary.
Retain the first failure while still awaiting every known retirement owner.

**Failure pattern:** cancelling an awaiter releases serialization or capacity while
its blocking worker, process or native provider continues; retries overlap, old
work writes into a new session, or shutdown waits for a worker while holding a
guard that worker needs to finish.

Name the owner of every task, timer, listener, subprocess, socket and permit.
Transfer required ownership into the actual work. Dropping an observer or timing
out a future is not evidence that external side effects stopped. Retain mutation
serialization and cleanup responsibility until real completion; bound admission
so repeated user retries cannot accumulate detached work.

A permit declared inside a blocking closure drops before the closure's remaining
captures. When those captures retain Node or storage handles, waking retirement
at that point can make close-before-reopen fail. Use the existing blocking work
owner in [runtime work](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/runtime_work.rs) for
[file/media maintenance](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/participant_runtime.rs),
so captures and undelivered results are destroyed before admission is released.
Keep the direct capture-drop ordering regression, queued cancellation and
undelivered-output controls, and the real native observer Node-release assertion;
do not narrow that assertion to conceal another producer retaining the profile.

A same-profile restart fixture must consume the existing retired storage close
before constructing its replacement. Joining producers through `stop()` alone
is not the fixture's proof that all Node and storage handles have closed. Keep
`stop_for_storage().await.close()` failure visible, including retained-handle
rejection, and preserve the subsequent durable reopen assertions. The shared
settings projection/restart scenario exercises this boundary with its old weak
application token still present; do not replace closure with a sleep or remove
the restart tail.

Follow the existing retirement protocol: close admission, signal cancellation,
release guards needed for completion, join owned tasks and drain admitted work.
Uncancellable native work needs an explicit ownership boundary: retain the
operation's serialization ownership, but not unrelated runtime/session guards across
the provider call. Revalidate publication and compensate stale effects through
the owner. A timeout is not permission to abandon durable work or reuse its slot.

**Evidence:** cancel the caller while work is paused; confirm retirement progress
where promised, retained serialization, eventual cleanup and absence of stale
publication. Include repeated cancellation and a successful noncancelled case.
See [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs) and the
runtime lifecycle boundaries in [module ownership](module-boundaries.md).

## R04: Deadlines cover the whole operation

## R03: Actual work owns its lifetime

Consume the canonical process owner's result contract rather than deriving a new
verdict from a diagnostic flag. Windows atomically terminates its owned job even
when empty, so verified `forcedRetirement` alone does not mean work leaked or a
successful test failed. Preserve the actual exit status and error, cancellation,
timeout and cleanup-verification results. The empty-job owner control and UI
runner outcome controls exercise that distinction.

POSIX process-group retirement proves only that group. A browser framework may
launch its web server in another group; use the actual tool's teardown protocol
and retain independent server-retirement controls in the UI command owner. Missing
cooperative teardown evidence cannot become verified cleanup merely because the
CLI exited or its group disappeared.
Tools such as Nextest and cargo-mutants create independently grouped children.
Killing their supervisor can close captured output while a real test remains
alive. Trace the tool's actual child ownership and shutdown protocol; neither
pipe closure nor the original group's disappearance proves retirement. The
[Linux mutation owner](../scripts/release/mutation-process-owner.py) uses a kernel
subreaper, pidfd-verified direct-child authority and one reaping loop across
normal exit and cancellation. Child enumeration supplies candidates, not absence
proof; only kernel `ECHILD` after reaping establishes no owned descendants.
Missing, invalid or incomplete retirement acknowledgment keeps cleanup unverified.
Reserve the owner's bounded teardown window without changing ordinary callers'
defaults or using process names, stale PIDs or broad group sweeps as authority.
Actual direct-tool, nested-tool and active-build cancellation controls retain an
unrelated sibling and require acknowledged test retirement before returning.

Leader exit and output-pipe closure are separate lifecycle events. Bound draining
after owned-group retirement: an escaped descendant can retain inherited pipes
forever. Close only the owner's read ends, retain unverified cleanup and quarantine
its lease; the real detached-pipe natural-exit and cancellation controls exercise
this failure in the validation process owner.
Cleanup uncertainty is monotonic across cancellation and draining: successfully
retiring one group cannot clear an earlier unverified escaped-process boundary.
Retain the first failure while still awaiting every known retirement owner.

**Failure pattern:** cancelling an awaiter releases serialization or capacity while
its blocking worker, process or native provider continues; retries overlap, old
work writes into a new session, or shutdown waits for a worker while holding a
guard that worker needs to finish.

Name the owner of every task, timer, listener, subprocess, socket and permit.
Transfer required ownership into the actual work. Dropping an observer or timing
out a future is not evidence that external side effects stopped. Retain mutation
serialization and cleanup responsibility until real completion; bound admission
so repeated user retries cannot accumulate detached work.

A permit declared inside a blocking closure drops before the closure's remaining
captures. When those captures retain Node or storage handles, waking retirement
at that point can make close-before-reopen fail. Use the existing blocking work
owner in [runtime work](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/runtime_work.rs) for
[file/media maintenance](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/participant_runtime.rs),
so captures and undelivered results are destroyed before admission is released.
Keep the direct capture-drop ordering regression, queued cancellation and
undelivered-output controls, and the real native observer Node-release assertion;
do not narrow that assertion to conceal another producer retaining the profile.

A same-profile restart fixture must consume the existing retired storage close
before constructing its replacement. Joining producers through `stop()` alone
is not the fixture's proof that all Node and storage handles have closed. Keep
`stop_for_storage().await.close()` failure visible, including retained-handle
rejection, and preserve the subsequent durable reopen assertions. The shared
settings projection/restart scenario exercises this boundary with its old weak
application token still present; do not replace closure with a sleep or remove
the restart tail.

Follow the existing retirement protocol: close admission, signal cancellation,
release guards needed for completion, join owned tasks and drain admitted work.
Uncancellable native work needs an explicit ownership boundary: retain the
operation's serialization ownership, but not unrelated runtime/session guards across
the provider call. Revalidate publication and compensate stale effects through
the owner. A timeout is not permission to abandon durable work or reuse its slot.

**Evidence:** cancel the caller while work is paused; confirm retirement progress
where promised, retained serialization, eventual cleanup and absence of stale
publication. Include repeated cancellation and a successful noncancelled case.
See [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs) and the
runtime lifecycle boundaries in [module ownership](module-boundaries.md).

name: Mutation Testing

# Pull requests, merge candidates and main pushes verify the pinned runner's
# real caught/survivor/baseline/hang/empty-selection behavior. Broad workspace
# mutation samples run daily or on explicit dispatch, independently of merging.
# Deep samples retain complete baselines, all consumers and strict reports.
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 4 * * *' # Daily deep assurance, outside the merge critical path
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: mutants-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  runner-contract:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-nextest@0.9.150
      - name: Verify pinned mutation runner behavior
        run: node --test scripts/diagnostics/mutants-workflow.test.mjs scripts/diagnostics/mutation-evidence.test.mjs scripts/release/run-mutants.test.mjs scripts/release/mutation-process-owner.test.mjs

  plan:
    name: Plan complete rotating mutation sample
    needs: runner-contract
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: '1'
    outputs:
      selected: ${{ steps.selection.outputs.selected }}
      matrix: ${{ steps.selection.outputs.matrix }}
      rust: ${{ steps.selection.outputs.rust }}
      node: ${{ steps.selection.outputs.node }}
      digest: ${{ steps.selection.outputs.digest }}
      producer_attempt: ${{ steps.selection.outputs.producer_attempt }}
      artifact_id: ${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-id }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-nextest@0.9.150
      - name: Select mutation sample
        id: selection
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: node ../scripts/release/run-mutants.mjs --plan "$RUNNER_TEMP/mutation-plan"
      - name: Preserve mutation plan
        id: upload
        if: always() && (steps.selection.outcome == 'success' || steps.selection.outcome == 'failure')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: mutation-plan-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/mutation-plan/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  baseline:
    name: Complete unmutated workspace baseline
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.selected != '0'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 80
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: '1'
      MUTATION_PLAN_DIGEST: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.digest }}
      MUTATION_PLAN_ATTEMPT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.producer_attempt }}
    outputs:
      digest: ${{ steps.baseline.outputs.digest }}
      producer_attempt: ${{ steps.baseline.outputs.producer_attempt }}
      artifact_id: ${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-id }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
